translations.Datly is an open-source analytics worksp: Datly is an open-source analytics workspace built on Microsoft Research’s Data Formulator. It combines natural-language exploration, visual chart controls, data threads, table inspection, and editable reports. The project is in beta.
translations.Does my data stay on my computer?: Does my data stay on my computer?
translations.A local installation processes transform: A local installation processes transformations on your computer. AI requests can include sample rows, field values, prompts, and tool outputs, which are sent to your configured model. If you select a cloud provider, that provider receives this context. A local model endpoint can keep model requests local; review your configuration and connected data sources.
translations.Does inspecting the table guarantee a co: Does inspecting the table guarantee a correct answer?
translations.No. The table helps you inspect the comp: No. The table helps you inspect the computed values, but AI can still choose an incorrect transformation, aggregation, or interpretation. Review the generated work, underlying data, and business assumptions before relying on a result.
translations.The code includes support for OpenAI, Az: The code includes support for OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, and local Ollama endpoints. You configure your provider and credentials. Model availability, capabilities, and any usage costs depend on that provider.
translations.Can I create reports and dashboards?: Can I create reports and dashboards?
translations.You can edit rich-text reports with char: You can edit rich-text reports with chart images, export a report image, or print to PDF. The current dashboard implementation saves chart references and displays title/type placeholders; a rendered, interactive multi-chart dashboard is not yet implemented.
translations.Datly’s source code is available under t: Datly’s source code is available under the MIT licence. Your model provider, connected infrastructure, or hosting may have their own costs. Check the repository’s setup instructions and releases for the current installation options.
